identity.resolvedIdentity: The three hand-operated Ørje locks between Rødenessjøen and Øymarksjøen, with associated lock residences, memorial, Ørje Brug and canal museum context.
identity.identityProblem: The combined name can be mistaken for the full Halden Canal, the museum, Ørje Brug or Ørje town centre.
identity.splitReason: The locks are the primary physical object; museum and industrial components remain secondary anchors in one coherent visitor environment.

evidence.finding: The named lock entity is located at 59.4814778, 11.6507861 and linked through Wikimedia Commons to Kulturminne ID 241336.
Marker municipality documents three hand-operated locks, approximately ten metres total lift, opening in 1860 and the associated lock residences and Engebret Soot memorial.
Ørje is one of three lock complexes in the approximately 80-kilometre Halden Canal system built for timber and transport infrastructure.
NVE identifies Ørje as the northern lock site and the canal museum as an adjacent interpretation institution.
The legacy point lies approximately 566.5 metres east of the named lock complex.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: This is the adjacent canal museum building, not the lock complex.
The town-centre point does not identify the locks.
Power and bridge infrastructure are separate objects.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted lock identity, canal-system scope, secondary museum anchor, rejected candidates and radius limits.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 566.5 metres west.
The lock complex is the primary anchor; the canal museum is secondary.
The full Halden Canal extends far beyond the gameplay circle.
